scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: People say a microwave cooks food from the inside out. It doesn't. So what actually happens?

scenes.name: mag
scenes.text: Inside, a part called a magnetron turns electricity into microwaves. Radio waves at about two point four five gigahertz.

scenes.name: box
scenes.text: A metal channel guides them into the box. The walls reflect them, so they bounce around the food, and the door mesh stops them escaping.

scenes.name: water
scenes.text: Water molecules have a plus end and a minus end. The wave's electric field flips billions of times a second.

scenes.name: heat
scenes.text: The molecules keep twisting to line up with it, bumping into their neighbours. That motion is heat.

scenes.name: depth
scenes.text: But microwaves only reach about one to two centimetres deep. The centre warms later, as heat spreads inward.

scenes.name: spin
scenes.text: Bouncing waves leave hot and cold spots, so the plate turns, and you're told to stir and let it stand.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Magnetron, waves, water, heat. Outside first, not inside. Follow for more on how things really work.
